headline: Dry, warm and breezy through Friday with gusty north-northeast winds Thursday and highs in the mid 80s in the LA valleys, while very high tides and a big swell bring a significant coastal flooding threat Wednesday and Thursday; light rain is possible Sunday night into Monday and a stronger storm is likely next Tuesday into Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Around Glendale and the LA basin, Wednesday and Wednesday night stay dry as a weakening cold front fizzles; only the Central Coast may see a few early-morning showers, with under 0.05 inch. Offshore winds from the north and east build through the day Wednesday in the usual Santa Ana wind spots of LA and Ventura Counties.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Offshore winds peak on Thanksgiving (Thursday), but with an unusually strong northerly push, meaning stronger north winds into the LA valleys and less wind in western Ventura County than in a typical Santa Ana. A Wind Advisory is in effect from 6 AM to 2 PM Thursday for the Santa Susana and western San Gabriel Mountains, and forecasters expect it may be expanded to the Santa Monica Mountains and valleys such as Santa Clarita, San Fernando and Simi. Friday morning will still be gusty, though advisories are much less likely, and with warm air aloft and downhill winds Friday is the warmest day, with highs in the mid 80s across the LA valleys.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The high pressure breaks down and shifts east this weekend, cooling temperatures to near normal by Sunday. The tail end of a storm aimed mainly at Northern California will likely bring some light rain Sunday night into Monday, mostly under half an inch. A stronger storm is likely next Tuesday into Wednesday, tapping subtropical moisture as a weak atmospheric river (a long plume of moisture streaming in from the Pacific), with about a 25 percent chance of a moderate-strength one; early guidance shows widespread totals of at least 1–2 inches, up to 5 inches in 6–8 hours on mountain slopes facing the incoming winds, some thunderstorm risk, and snow only above about 8,000 feet. With the very warm, record-breaking ocean temperatures and the heavy downpours from earlier storms, forecasters are concerned about flooding.

coast: The biggest concern this week is at the beaches. A large, long-period west swell peaks Wednesday and Thursday and combines with very high tides to bring large surf and moderate to significant coastal flooding, worst at high tide and in low-lying, unprotected spots. The highest surf and worst flooding are expected on the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, the Ventura County coast and far eastern parts of the southern Santa Barbara County coast, where Coastal Flood and High Surf Warnings run until noon Thursday; other beaches see somewhat lesser but still concerning impacts under Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories through Thursday, plus a Coastal Flood Watch for Thursday morning in some zones. Expect many strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, sneaker waves, heavy shore break, coastal erosion and risk of damage to coastal structures, making swimming dangerous. Offshore, Small Craft Advisories run through 3 PM Thursday, with outer-water seas peaking at 14–19 feet and north-of-Point-Sal inner-water seas at 13–17 feet on Wednesday; strong winds are expected in the western Santa Barbara Channel Wednesday and from Point Mugu to Santa Monica Thursday, with large breaking waves near harbor entrances that can capsize small boats.
watch_for: Significant coastal flooding and dangerous surf at high tide Wednesday and Thursday, worst on the Central Coast and Ventura County coast.
Gusty north winds Thursday in the LA valleys and mountains; the Wind Advisory may be expanded to the Santa Clarita, San Fernando and Simi Valleys.
The likely Tuesday–Wednesday storm: 1–2+ inches of rain with possible heavy downpours, flooding concerns and thunderstorms.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warm, windy weather through Friday and the coastal flooding threat; the Sunday night–Monday light rain and the stronger midweek storm are less certain but the latter looks likely.
